section_summary.extract_value: This section, titled 'Present Study', describes a single study investigating differences in gratitude, loneliness, subjective well-being, and health over 20 days among older individuals. Participants were assigned to either a gratitude condition (the 'three good things exercise') or a control condition. The study aimed to test four hypotheses concerning daily gratitude as a predictor of loneliness and health outcomes, condition differences in gratitude's impact, loneliness as a mechanism linking gratitude to health, and conditional indirect effects of loneliness based on experimental condition.
